articleTitle: Comparison of C4.5 Algorithms and Naive Bayes In Measuring Customer Satisfaction in Airlines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: The various activities of daily life cannot be separated from dependence on modes of transportation. Air transportation is one of the most important modes of transport. The airline industry is the one that acts as an air transportation service provider. As service providers, it is very important for them to pay attention to customer satisfaction. In 2023, the highest complaint of users as much as 56% was caused by lost luggage. On an average, other passenger complaints are caused by aircraft delays, operational reasons, and long transit times. Knowing the level of customer satisfaction can be used as a preference for improving service quality, so that customer loyalty that has been obtained can be maintained. The level of customer satisfaction on airlines can be determined by applying the C4.5 and Naïve Bayes algorithms, as well as the help of Rapidminer software. The C4.5 algorithm was chosen because it can present a large amount of data, which then results in a decision tree. The Naïve Bayes classification method was chosen because it is assumed to have the best performance compared with other types of classification methods. The data attributes used in this study included satisfaction level, age, class, flight distance, seat comfort, food and beverages, gate location, in-flight Wi-Fi service, ease of online booking, in-flight service, baggage handling, check-in service, cleanliness, and online boarding service. The results of this study indicate that the accuracy level of the C4.5 algorithm produces a better value than Naïve Bayes, with an accuracy difference of 4.94%; therefore, it can be concluded that the C4.5 algorithm is the best method for measuring the level of airline customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality Technologies in Mobile Applications To Optimize User Experience In Museum Tours
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: This article reviews modern approaches to the development and implementation of augmented reality (AR) technologies in mobile applications for museum tours and analyzes their advantages, difficulties of implementation, and prospects for further development in the context of increasing user engagement and satisfaction. The focus is on spatial methods that effectively integrate virtual objects into a user’s real environment. In particular, the use of simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) is grounded, which is an integral part of the augmented reality experience, provides geometric positioning of the augmented reality system, and extends the real environment by adding virtual objects based on the localization and structure of the environment. The integration of SLAM with GPS data to improve the positioning accuracy and real-time visual interaction with the environment is discussed.

articleTitle: Hyperparameter Tuning for Identifying Tree Seedling Mortality Using Logistic Regression on Environmental and Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Tree-seedling mortality is a significant challenge in forest management and agricultural practices, particularly in areas affected by climate change. The primary causes of seedling mortality are related to environmental factors and soil conditions. The early identification of these factors is crucial for improving seedling survival and land productivity. While existing studies have applied machine learning techniques to predict seedling mortality, they have often overlooked the importance of hyperparameter tuning in enhancing model performance. This study addresses this gap by focusing on the impact of hyperparameter tuning on the Logistic Regression models used to predict tree seedling mortality. Using a tree survival prediction dataset containing diverse environmental and soil factors, the model was optimized to achieve significant improvements. The tuned Logistic Regression model outperformed the standard approaches, achieving an accuracy of 93.71% and AUC of 97.81%. These results underscore the importance of hyperparameter optimization in boosting predictive accuracy, and demonstrate its potential to support improved forest conservation and management efforts more effectively than traditional models.

articleTitle: Onion Seedling Growth Optimization in Wates Village with Genetic Algorithm for Periodic Watering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Wates Village is one of the regions in Indonesia that is known for its agricultural activities. Onions are among the main commodities cultivated by farmers in this area. However, the growth of onion seedlings often faces various obstacles, such as a non-optimal watering process. An irregular watering process can lead to an imbalance in the water supply, which in turn can affect overall plant growth. To overcome this problem, the use of genetic algorithm-based technology can be an effective solution. The genetic Algorithm (AG) is an optimization method inspired by the process of biological evolution. It generates better solutions through iteration and selection based on certain criteria. By applying genetic algorithms, an optimal watering schedule can be determined by considering various factors such as weather conditions, soil type, and plant growth phase. The plants treated with AG had higher absolute growth (16.5 cm) than those without AG (15.1 cm). The percentage of growth from week to week was higher in plants with AG, especially in the first week (103.33% vs. 101.92%). The leaf number growth in plants with and without AG was similar in terms of absolute change (five leaves). However, the percentage of growth in the number of leaves in plants without AG was higher (250%) than that in plants treated with AG (166.67%).

articleTitle: Smart Driver Safety: Fatigue Detection Using YOLOv8 and Facial Landmarks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: This study aims to design and assess a driver fatigue detection model using YOLOv8, based on computer vision and facial landmarks. Driver fatigue is a leading cause of traffic accidents in Indonesia. Therefore, early detection is crucial for improving driving safety. The dataset contained images of the driver’s face in the awake and tired conditions. The data underwent preprocessing such as normalization, augmentation, and annotation to ensure consistency and sufficient variation. The YOLOv8 model was trained to compare its performance over 50 and 100 epochs. The results showed that the model with 100 epochs achieved impressive 96.1% precision, 96.3% recall, and 96.61% F1 score, instilling confidence in its effectiveness. The implementation of the model in video demonstrated effective real-time detection. Although this model provides good results, the use of face points has drawbacks under poor lighting conditions and unusual viewing angles. Thus, the YOLOv8 model has a significant potential for use in vehicle monitoring systems to improve road safety and reduce the risk of accidents caused by driver fatigue.

articleTitle: Customize Template Design And Verify Quick Response Code For Issuing E-Certificate
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: During the past Covid pandemic, the limitations of meetings or direct contact with many people made webinars a solution to keep conveying information to seminar participants. In the webinar, participants came and took part in the event online. This webinar format is often used in seminars, discussions, workshops, and talk shows. Almost all webinars provided electronic certificates (e-certificates) for participants, speakers, and organizers. E-certificates in the form of files and transmitted via the Internet make them vulnerable to counterfeiting; therefore, there needs to be an effort to secure the original data from the certificate owner and the activity data that issued the certificate. To maintain this aspect of data and information security, cryptography provides digital signature facilities that can guarantee authentication, data integrity, and nonrepudiation to eliminate fears of counterfeit certificates. The research system was developed using the RAD method, which is a systematic and sequential approach. In this application, users can design their own certificate templates to be provided to the participants. In addition to certificate design, the user can choose the logo position and signature location. Applications resulting from this research can also verify authenticity using Quick Response (QR) codes.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of MobileNET on Grape Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: The early identification of grapevine diseases is an important step in maintaining plant health and increasing yields. Grape vines are agricultural commodities with high economic value but are susceptible to various types of diseases. Disease detection technology using convolutional neural networks (CNN), one of which uses the MobilNet architecture, shows good results. This research aims to demonstrate the performance analysis of MobilNet in detecting diseases in grape leaves. The training process uses a dataset of 1600 images of leaves infected with three diseases: Black-Rot, Esca, leaf blight, and one healthy leaf. MobilNet was selected because of its high ability to classify images with limited computational resources. Thus, this method can help farmers implement preventive measures in a timely manner. MobilNet proved to be efficient and effective in detecting grape leaf diseases, achieving an average validation accuracy of 98% and a testing accuracy of 97%. This model can respond quickly to improve the quality and quantity of the grape harvest and prevent the spread of diseases in grape plants to minimize economic losses.

articleTitle: Road Pothole Damage Detector at Night Using YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: This study aimed to implement YOLOv8 Ultralytics to detect road potholes at night and analyze its accuracy under various lighting conditions. Detecting road potholes at night is crucial, because limited visibility increases the risk of accidents. Using data collected through web scraping and open sources, the model was trained on 3,685 images divided into 70% for training, 20% for testing, and 10% for validation. The results showed that the first scenario provided the best performance, with a precision of 83.0%, recall of 87.9%, and mAP50 of 89.9%. This indicates that the model can accurately detect more potholes. With an accuracy of 74.5% and an F1-Score of 85.4%, the first scenario offers an optimal balance between detection speed and precision, which is crucial in low-light conditions, such as at night.The main contributions of this study include the application of YOLOv8 for nighttime road pothole detection and the development of a real-time road-monitoring system to improve traffic safety. In the future, improvements can be made by expanding the data variation, such as adding poor weather conditions, and exploring additional sensors, such as Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), to enhance detection accuracy in complete darkness.

articleTitle: SRL Apps: The Support of ICT Adoption for Entrepreneurial Intention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Startup Readiness Level (SRL) apps were used to measure students’ level of business readiness. Student adaptation to SRL Apps needs to be evaluated to determine its impact on students’ entrepreneurial intention. The study was carried out by measuring factors that support student ICT adoption, namely perceived ease of use and level of application innovation. A quantitative survey was used as the research method. Questionnaires were distributed to 542 students who used SRL Apps. Data from the questionnaire were processed and analyzed using SmartPLS, and the analysis of research results was presented in line with the design of the research hypothesis. The test results from the research model presented findings that there was a positive impact from perceived ease of use and innovation, which was assessed by students on the ease of ICT adoption. The research results explain that entrepreneurial intention can be directly increased through ICT adoption of SRL Apps. The findings explain the importance of ICT adoption in business applications to support students’ interest in running a business. Clear measurements on SRL Apps are needed to evaluate student business achievements and to support student interest in continuing to run a business.

articleTitle: Advancements in Deep Learning Optimization for Post-Earthquake Building Damage Detection A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: This study conducts a systematic literature review (SLR) that focuses on optimizing deep-learning techniques for post-earthquake building damage detection. By employing the PRISMA protocol, this review aimed to collect, analyze, and summarize the findings of various studies published between 2014 and 2024. This research identifies and evaluates optimization methods such as hyperparameter tuning, transfer learning, and data augmentation, highlighting their effectiveness and implementation. Challenges such as data quality, computational costs, and model interpretability were also discussed. The findings indicate that while deep learning techniques significantly enhance the accuracy and efficiency of damage detection, further research is required to address existing challenges and improve model robustness in diverse earthquake scenarios.

articleTitle: Resampling and Ensemble Method for Enhance Breast Cancer Classification Performance in Imbalance Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Imbalance dataset cases are obstacles that can affect the classification performance. Classification models on imbalanced datasets tend to predict the majority class, which can cause a bias. In addition, the classification accuracy can be misleading. The Breast Cancer Wisconsin dataset is an imbalanced dataset in which the composition of the two classes is unbalanced. This study applied several methods for handling imbalanced datasets, including resampling techniques and ensemble methods. The results show that classification on datasets that apply resampling with the Undersampling and Oversampling methods has increased the performance of the Decision Tree method. The ensemble method with the balanced random forest classifier provides the highest accuracy value compared to the classification results on datasets without handling imbalanced datasets or on classification with resampling techniques. Although the accuracy value of the classification with the application of the resampling technique is still below the results of the balance-random forest, both resampling techniques provide very good time execution.

articleTitle: Bangladesh Software Industry: Factors Impacting On-Time Delivery in Hybrid Projects Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Software firms in Bangladesh face challenges integrating traditional values with modern project management methodologies. This blend aims to improve project outcomes and industrial growth through hybrid project management. This study identifies the critical factors influencing timely software project completion in Bangladesh and provides practical guidelines for enhancing hybrid project management practices. This study analyzes challenges such as skill gaps, communication barriers, inconsistent project lifecycles, budget constraints, inadequate capacity planning, cultural resistance, and regulatory compliance issues. This highlights small firms’ agility in adopting hybrid methodologies and the impact of project delays. The studies examine hybrid project management approaches that effectively address these challenges. Key solutions include advanced time estimation techniques, adaptive project management frameworks, enhanced stakeholder management tools, and improved resource management software that successfully integrate traditional values with modern methodologies in Bangladesh’s software industry. The research aims to provide actionable insights and practical guidelines to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of hybrid project management practices, ensuring on-time delivery and better project outcomes in the Bangladesh software sector.

articleTitle: Exploration of MBTI Personality Prediction through the Application of Traditional Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: All the various forms of social interaction do not avoid the tendency of each individual’s personality characteristics. With the increasing use of social media, the language patterns shown through posts are considered to be representative of a person’s personality traits, Therefore, this research will conduct personality prediction experiments using online forum post on the basis of the MBTI personality model. Our focus is to test how effective the use of traditional data augmentation is in helping to overcome the problem of data imbalance and its effect on the accuracy of the results. We used the three best models that have been used in previous studies, namely Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and a light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM). These experiments show that traditional data augmentation is still insufficient to provide the best results compared to synthetic data generation as done in previous studies. However, it still proves the need for augmentation data to help generalize the model with the best average results of 0.937 in Random Forest model training and 0.766 in SVM model testing, as well as an F1 with a score of 0.778 for the SVM model.

articleTitle: Analysis of Demand Forecasting in Upstream and Midstream Supply Chain Network of Sunflower Agro-industry Using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Sunflowers have high economic value because they can be processed into cooking oil and herbal oil, with by-products beneficial as animal feed. However, sunflower agribusiness in Indonesia lacks structured production and inventory planning, often relying on the intuition of owners or incoming orders. This study analyzes the demand for sunflower seed and oil products in the sunflower agro-industry using one-year historical sales data. The ANN method was used to predict the product demand for 250 mL, 500 mL, and 1 L packages. This research was conducted in sunflower fields in Banjaran and Cihanjuang, Bandung Regency. The results show that the ANN method provides more accurate demand forecasts than conventional methods. Accurate forecasting will help producers plan production and distribution more efficiently, thereby increasing the competitiveness of Indonesia’s sunflower agribusiness on a global scale. This study offers recommendations for sunflower seed and oil producers in planning production and distribution and helps improve agribusiness supply chain efficiency. These results are expected to serve as a reference for developing demand forecasting systems in other agribusiness sectors.

articleTitle: Implementation Monitoring Of Energy Harvesting For Electric Gear Motor Resources Using Rectenna, Solar And Dynamo Based On Android
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Technological developments in energy sustainability are receiving increasing attention, particularly in the use of electrical resources for various applications, including geared electric motors. Geared electric motors are key components of industrial automation systems, transportation, and other applications. To achieve optimal performance and efficiency, it is important to maintain a continuous supply of energy. Energy harvesting is becoming an important solution for increasing energy availability independently. It involves utilizing energy sources, such as electromagnetic radiation from rectennas, sunlight through solar panels, and kinetic energy from motion using dynamos. A combination of these sources can support the operation of a geared electric motor without relying on external power sources. Research has shown that the creation and monitoring of energy harvesting is key to developing a self-sufficient and efficient system. By integrating rectenna, solar, and dynamo technologies, an environmentally friendly and sustainable solution can be created to meet the energy requirements of geared electric motors. Effective monitoring is required to monitor system performance, detect potential failures, and optimize the use of the generated energy. The system operates in accordance with the planning of the research methodology. Testing the accuracy of the sensor shows that the lowest error value is 0% and the highest is 0.09%. Energy harvesting had an average of more than 5% higher than that using only solar panels. The application system can be used well on Android devices with 5+ series and above.

articleTitle: Android-based Community Supported Agriculture System for Grape Farmers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Grapes are one of the plantation commodities with a large potential in Indonesia because Indonesia has land that is suitable for growing grapes. Some challenges faced by grape farmers include pests and diseases, weather conditions, cultivation techniques, and limited access to information. By utilizing increasingly developed technology, it is hoped that it will make it easier for grape farmers to access information so that they can minimize the effects of existing challenges. This article discusses a system that aims to be a forum for the discussion and marketing of grape farmers. This system was created for the Android platform using the Kotlin programming language for data storage and the Firebase Firestore database. This system has a message exchange feature, a list of articles, a discussion column, and a catalog for marketing products from grape farmers. It is hoped that this system will help grape farmers face the challenges mentioned above.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Student Organization Chair Candidate Selection Using a Combination of ROC-MAUT and ROC-SMART
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: The selection of candidates for the student organization’s president is a crucial process that requires careful consideration to ensure effective and representative leadership. The problem is the potential for non-transparency in the assessment criteria and selection process, which can lead to dissatisfaction and distrust of other students. This study aims to compare the results of the combination of ROC-MAUT and ROC-SMART in the selection process for the election of candidates for the student council president in order to provide recommendations for the results of the comparison of methods used to be applied in the selection of candidates for student organization president candidates. The results of ranking comparison of the combination of ROC-MAUT and ROC-SMART methods show differences in ranking on two datasets, namely, on behalf of Reva Melda Satira with the ROC-MAUT method getting rank 2, with the ROC-SMART method getting rank 3, and on behalf of Ailia Lintang Maida with the ROC-MAUT method getting rank 3 and the ROC-SMART method getting rank 2. The results of the selection of candidates for the chairman of the organization in this study recommend a combination of the ROC-MAUT method compared to the ROC-SMART combination method because the results of the conformity level of the ROC-MAUT combination method have a value of 99.99546% higher than the ROC-SMART combination method, which obtains a value of 99.99521%.

articleTitle: A Novel QR-based Dimensionality Reduction Method for Malware Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Efficient and accurate categorization remains a pivotal challenge in the continuous struggle against malware. This paper proposes a novel strategy that employs a QR-based dimensionality reduction method designed for malware classification. By combining this methodology with artificial neural networks (ANNs), we achieved an accuracy rate of 98 % with only 10 reduced features of the BODMAS benchmark dataset. The proposed dimensionality reduction technique uses QR decomposition to effectively compress the feature space and optimize the input data while preserving crucial classification information. This drop increases the processing efficiency and speeds up neural network training. Our approach outperformed others in reliably recognizing and categorizing malware samples, as evidenced by rigorous testing. The findings demonstrate the potential of the QR-based technique as a foundational tool for improving the speed and reliability of malware detection.

articleTitle: The Essence of Perceived Compatibility and Behavioral Intention in Mobile Money Use
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Today, financial technology is a part of consumer needs. Mobile payments are used to support daily transactions, so a study of factors that can support behavioral intention and mobile money use is conducted. This study examines the support of digital literacy, perceived security, and perceived compatibility of mobile payments in increasing behavioral intention and mobile money use. The research was conducted on mobile payment users in Bandung City (Indonesia), and 416 research participants were asked using a questionnaire. The research was conducted using a quantitative survey and was processed using the SmartPLS tool. Two tests, namely, the PLS Algorithm and Bootstrapping, were used to test the research model. Next, the research hypothesis testing was used to explain the results. The research results found positive support from digital literacy, perceived security, and perceived compatibility on mobile payment behavioral intention. However, only perceived compatibility can directly increase the use of mobile money. In line with the hypothesis test, behavioral intention can support increased mobile money use by digital payment users. The research findings explain the ability of behavioral intention to mediate support for digital literacy, perceived security, and perceived compatibility in mobile money use.

articleTitle: Real-Time Graffiti Vandalism Detection: Enhancing Public Safety with the YOLOv8 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Graffiti vandalism, often considered a form of public expression, poses significant challenges to urban aesthetics and public safety. This study addresses the urgent need for effective real-time detection of graffiti vandalism using the YOLOv8 algorithm. The model was developed and evaluated across three distinct parameter scenarios, yielding a comprehensive comparison for identifying the optimal configuration for graffiti detection. Notably, Scenario 2 demonstrated the best performance, achieving a precision of 68,4% and recall of 65,4%, with a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.710. These quantitative metrics illustrate the effectiveness of the model for accurately detecting vandalism in various urban environments. By integrating a diverse dataset sourced from web scraping and existing open-source repositories, this study ensures robustness in detecting different graffiti types under various conditions. The findings indicate that the YOLOv8 model not only enhances the capability of authorities to monitor and manage graffiti effectively but also contributes to urban management systems by improving public safety and maintaining the aesthetic quality of public spaces.

articleTitle: Unveiling Serverless: A Systematic Review of Software Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Serverless architectures and Function as a Service (FaaS) are revolutionizing software development by allowing developers to focus on coding without managing infrastructure. This study explores the principles, challenges, and solutions related to serverless architecture and FaaS, focusing on their impact on developer experience and non-functional requirements (NFR) such as security, availability, and reliability. A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted to examine the primary approaches and their applications in serverless architectures, following established guidelines, in which 60 articles were selected from the 481 articles published in different digital sources between the years of 2013–2023. Serverless architectures enhance developer productivity and cost efficiency through pay-as-you-go models and autoscaling capabilities. However, challenges include cold-start latency, complex dependency management, security vulnerabilities, and reliability issues related to the stateless nature of functions and debugging difficulties. Serverless architectures and FaaS offer significant benefits in scalability and operational simplicity, and addressing security, availability, and reliability challenges is crucial. Ongoing research and innovation are essential for fully harnessing the potential of serverless computing.

articleTitle: Analysis of Consumer Behavior and Satisfaction of Self-Ordering Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Restaurants have a conventional and manual food ordering process that is considered ineffective because it takes a lot of time, and there is a chance of miscommunication caused by human error. The development of a self-ordering system allows customers to input orders by themselves so that the information goes to the kitchen directly. This research was taken from a case study at a fast-food restaurant because it examined the number of customers who wanted to buy food and queued up. This study aims to identify the factors that influence customer acceptance of self-ordering systems in Indonesian fast food restaurants. More than 300 data points were collected through questionnaires, using TAM as a reference for the research framework.

articleTitle: Construct and Dynamic Analyzing of a Novel Eight-Dimensional Hyperchaotic System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Chaos is often present in nonlinear systems, but not universally. This has led to extensive research focusing on identifying systems that can display chaos under certain parameters or initial conditions. Certain systems are notable for their complexity, owing to their high dimensionality and straight-forward nonlinear terms or parameter values. In this paper, we present and analyze a novel eight-dimensional hyperchaotic system constructed using nonlinear equations. The dynamical analysis results demonstrate that the novel hyperchaotic system has three large positive Lyapunov exponents. μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> = 22.072, μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> = 18.232, and μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> = 3.698, indicating a strong Perron effect. The Kolmogorov entropy of the system is 44.002, its Fractal Dimension is 6.584, and it has two unstable equilibrium points. Additionally, the 0–1 test results for all variables were close to 1, confirming the chaotic nature of the system. We also established the dissipation and sensitivity of the system to small changes in the initial conditions. MATHEMATICA simulations were employed to generate 2D and 3D phase and bifurcation diagrams, respectively. The analysis results show that the novel eight-dimensional hyperchaotic system outperforms many recently developed systems, including those with up to ten dimensions.

articleTitle: Automatic Face Detection Uses Deep Learning to Prevent Cheating in General Election
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: General elections are the cornerstone of a democratic system, where legitimacy and public trust are crucial for maintaining political stability and social welfare. In this context, challenges such as systematic fraud and the complexity of voter identification are primary concerns. This study analyzes the effectiveness of visual identity detection technology in ensuring electoral integrity and reducing fraud risk. Utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) as a part of Deep Learning (DL) is expected to address this issue. This study evaluated the visual identity detection system on a dataset of faces with varying perspectives and accessories. The test results showed that the model accurately recognized the faces, achieving an accuracy rate of approximately 90%. The analysis concludes that advanced research is needed for further development with more diverse datasets to enhance the accuracy in various complex situations. This study provides insights into the application of visual identity detection technology in general elections, aiming to contribute to strengthening public trust and security in the democratic process.

articleTitle: Hyperparameter Tuning Optimization on Machine Learning Models to Predict Software Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advanced Information Scientific Development (ICAISD)
abstract: Accessing and obtaining information has become seamless in the realm of software development. However, ensuring the software quality before deployment is crucial. This study focuses on evaluating software quality by identifying defects using predictive classification models. The study employs Ensemble Gradient Boosting techniques combined with hyperparameter optimization methods to enhance performance. Four optimization models were tested: Grid Search, Random Search, Bayesian Optimization (Hyperopt), and Optuna. The primary goal is to improve the prediction accuracy of software defects using various hyperparameter tuning approaches. The results demonstrated that Ensemble Gradient Boosting achieved a notable accuracy of 77.87% with an AUC of 0.777. In comparison, Grid Search achieved an accuracy of 68.79% and an AUC of 0.688, whereas Random Search recorded 67.80% accuracy and an AUC of 0.678. Hyperopt performed the best, yielding an accuracy of 79.36% and an AUC of 0.792. Optuna showed an accuracy of 68.54% with an AUC of 0.685. Among the models, Hyperopt emerged as the most effective, significantly improving accuracy and overall performance. This study highlights the impact of hyperparameter tuning in optimizing machine learning models for software defect prediction.
